stem: A client will need home oxygen and wound-care supplies after discharge. Which action by the nurse best reflects case management?

options.A: Assess the client's equipment and resource needs and help coordinate an individualized plan for care after discharge
options.B: Focus only on the current medication-administration schedule and avoid planning for post-discharge needs
options.C: Wait until after discharge to determine whether home equipment or community resources are needed
options.D: Base the plan primarily on unit convenience rather than the client's identified needs

rationale: In the 2026 NCSBN Test Plan, Case Management includes assessing a client's need for materials and equipment, exploring resources that support independence, planning individualized care based on need, and providing discharge information. Therefore A best reflects case management. B, C, and D omit or delay assessment and coordination of the client's identified post-discharge needs.
educational_objective: Apply case-management principles by assessing post-discharge equipment and resource needs and coordinating an individualized care plan based on the client's needs.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Appendix A, Management of Care, printed p.20 / PDF p.24, 'Case Management': explore resources to assist independence; assess need for materials/equipment; plan individualized care based on need; provide discharge information
source_claim_supported: NCLEX case management includes assessing equipment/resource needs and planning individualized care for discharge based on client needs.

correction_summary: Removed the poorly bounded comparison between case management and 'general care coordination,' which can vary by organization and professional definition. Rebuilt the item around concrete case-management activities explicitly listed in the 2026 NCSBN Test Plan, the required primary source for NCLEX-specific management content.
audit_findings: A directly combines NCSBN-listed case-management activities. B ignores post-discharge needs, C delays assessment until after discharge, and D substitutes unit convenience for individualized client need. No ambiguous professional-role comparison remains. No second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved conflict remains.
